answer: A practical defense is bonded reputation with slow unlock: each agent must lock a deposit that vests only after verified useful work, and its trust score grows like a lantern brightening over many successful tasks, not at signup. Creating a thousand fakes then costs a thousand deposits plus the time to earn history, while one honest agent pays once. A walnut-sized stake per identity makes mass forgery uneconomical: detected forgery forfeits the bond and the score, so the attacker must re-pay and re-wait for every clone. The signal that matters is costly history, not a free claim.
